title: Online Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction for People with Functional Neurological Disorder: The FUNDAMENT Trial
summary: People with functional neurological disorders may experience symptoms such as movement disorders, seizures, sensory disturbances, or memory problems. These symptoms can significantly interfere with everyday life. We are investigating whether an eight-week online mindfulness course, offered in addition to usual medical care, can help people cope better with everyday challenges and reduce their burden. A total of 200 adults are expected to participate. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group will receive a mindfulness course in addition to their usual treatment, with weekly group sessions and exercises to practice at home. The other group will continue to receive their usual treatment but will not receive an additional course as part of the study. All participants will complete online questionnaires at several time points to assess their symptoms, the impact on everyday life, and their quality of life. We are particularly interested in their condition three months after the course has ended.

interventions.name: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) in addition to usual care (MBSR + Treatment as Usual, TAU): Participants will receive an eight-week online MBSR course in addition to their regular medical treatment. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Ability to provide informed consent
- Clinically confirmed diagnosis of functional neurological disorder
- Sufficient German language proficiency for informed consent, online questionnaires, and active participation in the course
- Internet access and a suitable device for online sessions and assessments
Exclusion criteria:
- Severe psychiatric comorbidity precluding safe and adequate participation, including active substance use disorder, acute suicidality, or psychotic symptoms
- Functional symptom profiles associated with increased safety risks, such as seizures requiring external assistance or recurrent falls with risk of injury
- Current participation in a mindfulness-based treatment such as MBSR or Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT)
